cards.back: The spread of observations around their mean in a sample or population model.
The uncertainty scale of an estimator across repeated samples; for a mean, approximately s/√n under independence.
The precisely defined quantity a study aims to estimate, such as a treatment effect in a target population.
A quantitative measure of the magnitude of a difference or association.
Probability under a specified null model of data at least as extreme as observed, subject to the test assumptions.
The expected fraction of false positives among rejected hypotheses under a specified multiple-testing procedure.
Treating non-independent subsamples as independent experimental replicates.
Grouping experimental units by a nuisance factor so treatment comparisons are made within more homogeneous groups.

cards.front: The vehicle mean is 10.0 μM and the compound mean is 14.0 μM. What is the compound-minus-vehicle sample contrast?
cards.back: The observed contrast is +4.0 μM. It summarizes the two samples; it does not imply that every compound replicate was higher.

cards.front: Why are two group means alone insufficient to establish statistical uncertainty or causation?
cards.back: Uncertainty needs replicate-level variability and dependence information. Causal interpretation also needs assignment details; the means alone provide neither.

cards.front: What information is lost when a graph shows group means without replicate values or uncertainty intervals?
cards.back: The mean-only plot hides within-group spread and the precision of each estimate; it cannot by itself show sampling uncertainty or establish a causal effect.
A censored subject was event-free for the time observed; keep them in the risk set until censoring and do not count an event.
S(t) is the product of (1 − d/n) over event times up to t, with n the number at risk just before each event.
Events per person-time ratio estimates a hazard ratio if hazards are roughly constant; a single HR misleads when curves cross.
If subjects leave because of the outcome, censoring is informative and the estimate is biased; report why subjects were censored.
